technical_body.os: X11 (release 15-25 covered classical era); Linux-underlay 'PDT' on CS1000 R4+
technical_body.craft_interface: Numbered overlays ('LD nn' -> loads program nn). Prompt is '>'. Commands are 3-4 letter mnemonics: PRT, NEW, CHG, OUT, END. Exit an overlay with '****'.
access_channels: SDI (Serial Data Interface) TTY port on the CPU — direct RS-232
MSDL (Multi-purpose Serial Data Link) card — successor to SDI, often at 9600 baud
Dial-in modem on the SDI/MSDL — 300/1200/2400 bps typical, sometimes 9600. Frequently on an unpublished DID range. This is the phreak-relevant entry point.
PDT (Problem Determination Tool) via SSH on CS1000 R4+ (era 2005+, out of classic-phreak scope)
technical_body.notes: Newer generics forced password change on first login but many sites did not. LD 22 dumps installed packages so an attacker knows which features are licensed.

technical_body.role: Class-5 (local) and Class-4/5 combo digital switch. Dominant AT&T local switch of the 1980s-2000s.
technical_body.craft_interface: RC/V (Recent Change / Verify) terminal. Prompt '<'. Menu tree navigated by numeric codes: 1.1 = line data, 1.2 = trunk data, 8.1 = call-forwarding features, 8.6 = custom calling, 12.1 = screening/restrictions.
technical_body.load_verify_pattern: '4>0' starts a recent-change session, '4>2' verifies, '4>3' executes. Unexecuted changes leave an audit trail.
technical_body.trap_trace: The 5ESS TRACE command is live-callable from RCV. A 5ESS you're touching can log your session in real time.
technical_body.notes: The '<' prompt on a scanned modem line is the strongest single fingerprint for a 5ESS RCV port.

technical_body.role: DMS-10 (small local), DMS-100 (Class-5 local), DMS-200 (Class-4 toll/access-tandem), DMS-250 (IXC toll switch — Sprint's backbone).
technical_body.craft_interface: MAPCI (Maintenance and Administration Position Command Interpreter). Prompt 'CI:'. Navigated by nested menus + commands: MAPCI -> MTC (maintenance) -> TRKS (trunks) -> TTP (trunk test position).
key_sub_cis: SERVORD — service order (add/change subscriber lines). Commands: NEW, CHF (change features), OUT, NEWACD.
TABLE — direct access to translation tables (OFCVAR, OFCENG, OFCOPT, OFCSTD, CLLI, TRKGRP, LENLINES).
LTP (Line Test Position) — seize/test a subscriber line, apply milliwatt.
TTP — seize/test a trunk; can monitor active calls on old generics with 'permit CI TTP MONITOR'.
LOGUTIL — the switch's log. Also the thing to disable to cover tracks.
technical_body.backchannel: DMS switches in Canada were reachable via NT's private X.25 'Datapac' back-network.
